evals.name: purchase-invoice-amount-drift-cross-repo
evals.prompt: our purchase invoice totals keep drifting when someone changes the ledger account on a line — the invoice ends up worth less than the supplier actually billed. i genuinely don't understand where these amounts even get calculated. is it in the blazor frontend or in the api? it's a black box to me. can you explain the whole flow, from the AI reading the PDF through to the journal posting, and tell me where the problem actually is?
evals.expected_output: A published artifact explaining that the arithmetic lives in a shared library both sides call, that the caller chooses the split direction, and that splitting from net makes the gross an output — traced through the header total to the journal's supplier row, with diagrams and real file paths.
evals.notes: Requires three repos on disk: a Blazor frontend, a .NET backend, and an AI extraction service. The point of this case is that the answer spans all three and the naive answer picks one side.
assertions: Published a Claude artifact and returned its URL
Answered the user's literal question: the arithmetic is neither frontend nor backend, it is a shared library both sides call
Reached all three repositories, not only the frontend
Stated where code executes, distinguishing the browser from the server
Separated the code that computes from the code that chooses the direction of the split
Identified the mechanism: splitting from net makes the gross an output
Traced the consequence through the header total to the journal's supplier row
Cited concrete file paths that exist in the repositories
Told the user the artifact is private and needs sharing
